Ballot Measure Rebuttal Argument Submission Form
If both an argument in favor of an argument against a measure have been selected for publication in the Sample
Ballot & Official Voter Information Pamphlet, a typed rebuttal to the argument in favor of or the argument against the
measure may be submitted as outlined in this form.
The author(s) of the primary argument of the measure may prepare and submit a rebuttal argument or may authorize
in writing any other person or persons to prepare, submit or sign the rebuttal argument.
A rebuttal argument will not be accepted unless accompanied by this completed form, which shall contain the printed
name(s) and signature(s) of the person(s) submitting it or, if submitted on behalf of a bona fide association of citizens,
the name of the association and the printed name and signature of at least one of its principal officers. Please make
sure you are using proper format before submitting to the Elections Office.
Word count limit for Rebuttal Arguments 250 words

Rebuttal to Argument Against Measure T
Measure T is not a new tax; Yes on Measure T renews existing funding dedicated to programs
such as 5th grade Outdoor Education, library services for all students, and a mental health
counselor. If Measure T does not pass, we will have to cut an additional $1.4 million from our
Accountability safeguards such as a citizens' oversight committee, public spending disclosures,
and annual audits have and will continue to ensure responsible use of these dedicated funds.
Pacifica schools are consistently among the lowest-funded per student, forcing teachers and
classified staff to repeatedly fight for fair compensation. In San Mateo County, an annual income
of $117,500 for an individual is considered low income, yet Pacifica teachers start at just
$57,000, while classified staff and librarians earn even less.
Pacifica students need thriving local educators, not a revolving door of teachers leaving our
community for a living wage in other districts. If we expect students to perform better in school,
we must retain qualified teachers, preserve counselors and librarians. Libraries play a critical
role in building literacy, strengthening reading comprehension, and giving students the skills
they need to succeed across every subject.
The author of the argument against Measure T does not live in the Pacifica community, routinely
opposes school ballot measures and cherry-picks facts. He doesn't have students in our
schools, and he should not speak for Pacificans. We can give Pacifica's children the strong
educational foundation they deserve by voting Yes on Measure T.
